metadata.description: Comprehensive, multi-language regex pattern bank for static entity detection in device UI screenshots. Covers phone screens across all application types and car/vehicle HMI screens, with language coverage spanning Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai, and CJK scripts. Each pattern maps a structured text format to its entity type and provides a classification signal (system vs user text) plus a confidence score for downstream thresholding.
metadata.usage: Load with json.load(), compile each regex with re.compile(pattern['regex'], re.IGNORECASE) where case_insensitive is true (else flags=0 — several non-Latin-script patterns are intentionally case_insensitive=false since case doesn't apply), then run re.search(compiled, text_block) on each OCR transcribed_text. Matched patterns provide entity_type and classification signal. 'confidence' is a static prior; combine with your OCR confidence and surrounding UI context (app category, screen region) for a final redaction decision. Patterns flagged in 'notes' as collision-prone should be weighted down or required to co-occur with a contextual anchor before acting on them.
coverage: Phone: messaging, email, banking, ride-sharing, social media, navigation, music/media, shopping, food delivery, travel, health/fitness, weather, calendar, settings, phone/dialer, browser, camera, clock, calculator, notes, government/ID services, crypto wallets, security/2FA prompts

Car: dashboard, instrument cluster, navigation, infotainment, phone integration, climate control, ADAS/safety, tire pressure, OBD diagnostics, EV charging, drive mode/gear/cruise control, Android Auto, Apple CarPlay
language_script_coverage: Latin: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Indonesian, Swedish, Danish, Polish, Czech, Turkish, Romanian, Hungarian, Vietnamese

categories.name: Email Address
categories.description: Email addresses found in profile screens, contact lists, account settings, messaging apps, login forms. Format is language-agnostic (ASCII local-part is the overwhelming global norm; IDN/unicode domains are rare in UI screenshots).

patterns.description: Human-obfuscated email address as seen in bios/profiles ('name [at] domain [dot] com')
patterns.notes: Common in social media bios to dodge scraper bots; still PII.

categories.name: Phone Number
categories.description: Phone numbers across formats: contacts, profile screens, ride-sharing, banking support, incoming calls on car screens. Includes E.164/international style plus common domestic groupings for major markets (US/CA, UK, France, Germany, Japan, and generic grouped-digit fallback).

patterns.description: International phone number with + country code (covers US +1, EU +33/+44, Asia +81/+91, etc.)
US/CA phone number with area code in parentheses
US/CA phone number with dashes or dots (no parentheses)
US/CA toll-free numbers (800, 888, 877, etc.) — typically support lines
patterns.notes: Toll-free numbers are typically system-provided support lines, not personal user data

patterns.description: UK domestic phone number (landline or mobile, leading trunk 0)
French domestic phone number (10 digits in pairs, leading 0)
German domestic phone number (area/mobile code + subscriber number)
patterns.notes: Broad format range for DE numbering; can overlap with other grouped digits, context matters.

patterns.description: Japanese domestic phone number (mobile or landline, hyphenated)
Generic grouped-digit phone-like number, catch-all fallback for locales not covered above
patterns.notes: Low-confidence fallback; prone to collisions with other grouped numerics (order/ref numbers). Prefer a locale-specific match when available.

categories.name: Time Display
categories.description: Time shown on status bars, clocks, navigation ETA, alarm apps, calendar events, car dashboard clocks. Numeric HH:MM is near-universal across locales; two informal written variants (French 'Xh Y', Japanese kanji) are added since they don't reduce to plain HH:MM.

patterns.description: 24-hour time display (also matches bare clock times like 8:43, 12:32, 14:22)
patterns.notes: Lower confidence because bare HH:MM can also appear in durations or scores. When the entire text block is just this pattern, confidence is higher.

patterns.description: Time with seconds (stopwatch, timer, video timestamp, detailed clock)

patterns.notes: Can collide with height/other 'h' unit mentions; moderate confidence.

patterns.description: Chinese time notation using 点/分 (HH点MM分)

categories.name: Date Display
categories.description: Dates on receipts, transactions, calendar, messages, notifications, trip history, booking confirmations. Numeric formats are locale-agnostic; month-name and relative-date ('today/yesterday') formats are language-specific, so this category carries one pattern per major language/script cluster (Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Devanagari, CJK, Thai).

patterns.description: English date, day first: '24 October 2026', '29th July 2026'
German date, 'D. MONAT (JJJJ)' — note the period after the day number
Swedish date, 'D MÅNAD (ÅÅÅÅ)' — spelling largely shared with Norwegian Bokmål
patterns.notes: Norwegian Bokmål month names are near-identical; this pattern also catches most Norwegian dates.

patterns.description: Polish date, genitive month form: 'D MIESIĄCA (RRRR)'
Czech date, genitive month form: 'D. MĚSÍCE ROK'

patterns.notes: Hungarian uniquely orders year-month-day; pattern reflects that.

patterns.description: Russian date, genitive month form (Cyrillic): 'D МЕСЯЦА (ГГГГ)'

patterns.regex: \d{1,2}\s+(?:มกราคม|กุมภาพันธ์|มีนาคม|เมษายน|พฤษภาคม|มิถุนายน|กรกฎาคม|สิงหาคม|กันยายน|ตุลาคม|พฤศจิกายน|ธันวาคม)(?:\s?\d{4})?
patterns.description: Thai date, Thai month names (year often given in Buddhist Era, +543 vs Gregorian)
Vietnamese date, 'ngày D tháng M năm YYYY'
Chinese/Japanese numeric date using 年/月/日 (YYYY年M月D日)
Numeric date with slashes (MM/DD/YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY)
Date with dots (common in EU/DE/RU: DD.MM.YYYY)
patterns.notes: Can conflict with version numbers or IP fragments. Context matters.

patterns.description: English day of week, optionally with date (calendar, schedule, notifications)

patterns.regex: (?:Today|Yesterday|Tomorrow|\d+\s+(?:min(?:ute)?s?|hours?|days?|weeks?|months?)\s+ago|Just now|Last\s+(?:week|month|year)|This\s+(?:week|month|year)|Hoy|Ayer|Mañana|Manana|hace\s+\d+\s+(?:segundos?|minutos?|horas?|d[ií]as?|semanas?|meses?)|ahora mismo|Aujourd'hui|Hier|Demain|il y a\s+\d+\s+(?:secondes?|minutes?|heures?|jours?|semaines?|mois)|à l'instant|Heute|Gestern|Morgen|vor\s+\d+\s+(?:Sekunden|Minuten|Stunden|Tagen|Wochen|Monaten)|gerade eben|Oggi|Ieri|Domani|\d+\s+(?:secondi|minuti|ore|giorni)\s+fa|proprio ora|Hoje|Ontem|Amanhã|Amanha|há\s+\d+\s+(?:segundos?|minutos?|horas?|dias?)|agora mesmo|Vandaag|Gisteren|\d+\s+(?:seconden|minuten|uur|dagen)\s+geleden|zojuist|Сегодня|Вчера|Завтра|\d+\s+(?:секунд|минут|часов|дней)\s+назад|только что|今日|昨日|明日|\d+分前|\d+時間前|たった今|今天|昨天|明天|\d+分钟前|\d+小时前|刚刚|오늘|어제|내일|\d+분\s*전|\d+시간\s*전|방금)
patterns.description: Relative date/time expressions across major languages, used in notifications, messages, social feeds
patterns.notes: Combines bare today/yesterday/tomorrow terms with each language's own '...ago'/'just now' construction rather than assuming English syntax; some overlap risk with unrelated short words is mitigated by requiring the full token.

categories.name: Time Duration
categories.description: Duration displays in navigation ETA, call length, music playback, workout timers, cooking apps, download estimates. English patterns kept granular by unit; other languages combined per-language since unit words are short and collide less.

patterns.description: Duration in seconds (timers, loading, short durations)
Duration in days (delivery estimates, countdowns, subscriptions)

patterns.notes: 'ora/ore' can collide with unrelated short words; combined with a leading digit to reduce false positives.

patterns.description: Duration unit, Russian (handles common case endings)
Duration unit, Chinese/Japanese (shared CJK characters for sec/min/hour/day)
patterns.notes: Single characters like 分/日 are short and can appear in unrelated compounds; digit-adjacency required to reduce noise.
Single-syllable units are short; digit-adjacency required to reduce noise.

categories.name: Currency / Money Amount
categories.description: Monetary values in banking apps, shopping, ride-sharing receipts, food delivery, payment confirmations, pricing, tipping. Covers symbol-prefixed, symbol-suffixed (common in EU formatting), and ISO-code forms.

patterns.description: Dollar amount with $ symbol (USD, CAD, AUD, etc.)
Euro amount with € symbol, prefix position
Euro amount with € symbol, suffix position (common in DE/FR/IT/ES/NL receipts)
Japanese Yen or Chinese Yuan with ¥ symbol
Indian Rupee with ₹ symbol (uses lakh/crore grouping)
Amount followed by ISO 4217 currency code
Other currency symbols (Won, Peso, Dong, Hryvnia, Tenge, Lira, Manat, Ruble)
Amount followed by a spelled-out currency name
patterns.notes: Spelled-out currency words are more collision-prone than symbols/codes; treat as supporting evidence.

categories.name: Distance Measurement
categories.description: Distance values on navigation screens, ride-sharing apps, maps, fitness trackers, car dashboards, delivery apps. Unit abbreviations (km, mi, m, ft, yd, cm) are used near-universally in UI even on localized apps, so no separate per-language variants are needed beyond the addition of centimeters for close-range sensors.

patterns.description: Distance in miles (negative lookahead prevents matching 'min')
Distance in meters (spelled out to avoid single 'm' false positives)
Distance in centimeters (parking sensors, close-range car proximity displays)

categories.name: Speed Measurement
categories.description: Speed displays on car dashboards, navigation screens, speedometers, fitness tracking (running pace).

categories.name: Temperature
categories.description: Temperature on weather apps, car climate control, cabin temperature, thermostat, cooking apps.

patterns.description: Temperature in Fahrenheit with degree symbol
Temperature in Celsius with degree symbol
Temperature with degree symbol but no unit letter (common on car displays). Negative lookahead excludes compass bearings.
patterns.notes: Lower confidence because bare degree could be compass bearing. Negative lookahead for N/S/E/W helps disambiguate.

categories.name: Percentage Value
categories.description: Battery level, download progress, signal strength, humidity, health stats, discount percentages, volume level.

categories.name: Financial Identifiers
categories.description: Masked/full card numbers, account references, transaction IDs, routing codes found in banking, payment, and receipt screens.

patterns.description: Masked card/account number with bullet dots
Full card format with middle digits masked
Full unmasked 16-digit payment card number (Visa/Mastercard/Discover, grouped 4-4-4-4)
patterns.notes: High-sensitivity PII; unmasked full PANs should almost never legitimately appear in a screenshot — flag for redaction with high priority.

patterns.description: Full unmasked American Express card number (15 digits, grouped 4-6-5)
patterns.notes: Amex uses a distinct 4-6-5 grouping unlike the 4-4-4-4 grouping of most other networks.

patterns.description: Card brand name followed by last digits
Order number with hash prefix (shopping, food delivery)
IBAN (International Bank Account Number). BBAN segment is alphanumeric (not purely numeric) since several countries — the UK among them — embed a bank code made of letters.
SWIFT/BIC bank identifier code (8 or 11 characters)
patterns.notes: 8-char alphanumeric codes are collision-prone with other short codes; treat as low-confidence unless near banking context.
Same shape as some date formats (DD-MM-YY); banking-app context increases confidence.

patterns.description: US ABA bank routing number, label-anchored to avoid matching bare 9-digit strings
Ethereum-style wallet address (also used by many EVM-compatible chains)

categories.name: Road / Highway Code
categories.description: Road designations on navigation and map screens (car and phone navigation apps).

patterns.description: European road codes (E-15, AL-3302, A-1050, N-340, AP-7)
US road codes (Interstate, US Route, State Route, County Road, Highway)
UK motorway/A-road codes (M25, A1, M1, A40)
patterns.notes: Single letter+number patterns have moderate confidence due to possible false positives
Overlaps in shape with UK codes and generic letter+number tokens; disambiguate with locale context.

patterns.regex: [東名阪中国九州東北関越]{1,3}自動車道|首都高速\d{0,2}号?
patterns.description: Japanese expressway names (kanji), e.g. Tomei/Meishin/Shuto expressways
Highway exit numbers (multilingual: EN, FR, ES, DE, IT, PT, NL, PL, RU)

categories.name: Network / Connectivity Indicator
categories.description: Cellular and wireless indicators on phone status bars and car infotainment connectivity panels. Abbreviations are used unchanged across virtually all locales.

patterns.notes: Free-text SSID value has no fixed shape; the label is the reliable anchor.

categories.name: Vehicle Telemetry & Diagnostics
categories.description: Car dashboard readings: RPM, tire pressure, voltage, fuel efficiency, OBD codes, VIN, odometer, engine data, and consumable/service-life indicators.

patterns.description: OBD-II diagnostic trouble code (Powertrain, Chassis, Body, Network)
Vehicle Identification Number (17 alphanumeric characters, excludes I, O, Q)
patterns.notes: 17 chars can match other alphanumeric strings. Verify context.

patterns.description: Fuel efficiency in miles per gallon
Fuel efficiency in liters per 100km (European standard)
EV charging power rate or energy capacity
Consumable/service-life percentage indicator (oil life, brake pads, tires)

patterns.regex: (?:Fasten\s+(?:your\s+)?seatbelt|Please\s+fasten\s+seat\s?belt|Attachez\s+(?:votre\s+)?ceinture|Bitte\s+(?:Sicherheitsgurt\s+)?anschnallen|Abroche(?:se)?\s+el\s+cintur[oó]n|Allacciare\s+(?:le\s+)?cintur[ae]|シートベルトを締めてください|请系好安全带|안전벨트를\s*착용)
patterns.description: Seatbelt warning text across major languages
examples: シートベルトを締めてください

patterns.description: Low fuel warning text across major languages

categories.name: Media & Entertainment
categories.description: Radio frequency, ratings, resolution on music players, radio apps, video apps, app stores, review platforms.

patterns.description: Rating as fraction (app stores, reviews, restaurants)

categories.name: Data Size & Transfer Speed
categories.description: File sizes, storage usage, download/upload speeds on settings, file managers, browser, speed tests, cloud storage.

patterns.description: Network transfer speed in bits per second
Network transfer speed in bytes per second
Data usage as used/total (storage, data plans)

categories.name: Health & Fitness Metrics
categories.description: Health readings on fitness trackers, health apps, smartwatch displays, medical apps.

patterns.description: Heart rate in beats per minute

patterns.notes: Can conflict with date fractions or scores. Context important.

patterns.description: Blood glucose reading in mg/dL (glucose monitor apps)
Blood glucose reading in mmol/L (glucose monitor apps, non-US)
Sleep duration reading from a sleep-tracking app

categories.name: Navigation & Location Data
categories.description: GPS coordinates, compass bearings, altitude, ETA markers on navigation and map apps (phone and car). Includes 'ETA' label translated for major languages.

patterns.description: GPS coordinates in decimal degrees (latitude, longitude)
GPS coordinates in degrees/minutes(/seconds) — seconds component is optional since coarser DM-only displays are common
Altitude in meters (requires unit context word to avoid matching plain meters)
Compass bearing with degrees and direction
ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) with time value
Turn-by-turn navigation instruction across major languages

categories.name: Weather Data
categories.description: Weather metrics displayed in weather apps, car dashboards, notification widgets.

patterns.description: Wind speed (overlaps with speed category but paired with wind context)

categories.name: Software & Product Identifiers
categories.description: Version numbers, build numbers, serial numbers, model numbers found in settings, about screens, app stores.

patterns.notes: Device-identifying, not personally-identifying, but still worth flagging in security-sensitive contexts.

categories.name: Social Media Markers
categories.description: Social media handles, hashtags, mentions found across social and messaging apps.

patterns.description: Social media handle/mention (Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok, etc.)

categories.name: URL / Web Address
categories.description: URLs and web addresses in browser, messaging, email, link sharing, app screens.

patterns.notes: URLs are typically system-displayed links, but user could have typed/pasted them

patterns.description: URL starting with www (no protocol prefix)
Internationalized domain name in Punycode form

categories.name: Network Addresses
categories.description: IP and MAC addresses in network settings, diagnostics, developer tools, router apps.

patterns.description: IPv6 address, full or abbreviated with a single '::' zero-run contraction anywhere in the address
patterns.notes: Abbreviated forms can be short; combine with network-settings context to reduce false positives.

categories.name: Postal / ZIP Code
categories.description: Postal codes found in address fields, delivery apps, ride-sharing, profile forms, shipping labels, across major postal-code formats worldwide.

patterns.notes: Low confidence because bare 5-digit numbers are common. Higher confidence when in address context.
Shape overlaps with other 2-3 digit dashed codes; address context increases confidence.
Bare 6-digit numbers are highly collision-prone (phone fragments, OTPs, IDs); needs address context.

patterns.description: Label-anchored postal code in any format (English/Spanish/French/German)

categories.name: One-Time Passwords & PIN Codes
categories.description: Verification codes shown in SMS/authenticator notifications, banking app 2FA screens, and PIN entry prompts. Extremely high-value to redact since exposure enables account takeover.

patterns.description: Labeled PIN/passcode entry (banking, phone unlock, safe/lock apps)

categories.name: Messaging Status Labels
categories.description: System-generated status text in messaging/chat apps (delivery/read receipts, presence indicators). Useful to classify as 'system' signal so redaction tools don't over-flag routine chrome text as personal content.

patterns.notes: Common English words; combine with messaging-app UI context to avoid over-matching prose.

patterns.regex: \b(?:Entregado|Le[ií]do|Escribiendo\.\.\.|En l[ií]nea|Livr[ée]|Lu|En train d'[ée]crire|En ligne|Zugestellt|Gelesen|Tippt gerade|Online|Consegnato|Letto|Sta scrivendo|Entregue|Lida|Digitando|Bezorgd|Gelezen|Aan het typen)\b|(?:已送达|已读|正在输入|既読|送信済み|入力中|전송됨|읽음|입력\s*중)

categories.name: Emergency Service Numbers
categories.description: Emergency dial numbers as shown on phone dialer/SOS screens and car SOS/eCall systems. Context-anchored to avoid matching arbitrary short numbers.

patterns.notes: Bare 2-3 digit emergency codes are too collision-prone to match without an anchoring label like 'Emergency' or 'SOS'.
